terms.comment: The strongest general word for a wicked act (Lewis & Short). To commit a crime, scelus committere (Traupman 194) or admittere (Cic. Att. 9.10.3, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a misdeed, a crime; in comedy also simply a deed

terms.comment: The law’s word for a criminal act, as in Cicero’s pūniendōrum maleficiōrum causā.

terms.gloss: a crime (mostly in poets and later prose); classically the charge
terms.comment: Above all the accusation (see charge); the sense ‘crime’ is rare in prose before Augustus (Lewis & Short). Traupman: “more often means merely the charge”.

phrases.latin: Facinus est vincīre cīvem Rōmānum, scelus verberāre, prope parricīdium necāre
phrases.english: It is a crime to bind a Roman citizen, a wickedness to flog him, almost parricide to kill him

phrases.latin: ex eā cāritāte quae est inter nātōs et parentēs, quae dirimī nisi dētestābilī scelere nōn potest
phrases.english: the love between children and parents, which nothing but a hateful crime can break
